newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma delays Turkmen trip over gas debt.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma delays Turkmen trip over gas debt.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma has postponed a trip to Turkmenistan scheduled for Monday, when he was due to sign a long-term natural gas supply deal, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.
"The president will not be leaving for Turkmenistan today," the spokesman told Reuters, giving no reason for the delay.

But Interfax-Ukraine news agency quoted Anatoly Mynchenko, a state minister for energy, as saying on Sunday that the decision was taken after Ashgabat sent a note on Friday proposing that a $205-million debt for 1996 gas deliveries be settled first, and a system of direct supplies be set up.

Mynchenko was quoted as saying that the Ukrainian government bore no responsibility for the $205-million worth of Turkmen natural gas imported last year by Itera-Ukraine, a joint venture with Itera International Energy Corp.
But he added that the government could help organise payment of the debt.
Under a government-sponsored scheme set up in 1995, but since slammed by Kuchma as uncompetitive, private and state companies are selected to supply gas to Ukraine and collect debts.
Ashgabat cut gas supplies to Ukraine in March, and only renewed them after Kiev put state-owned gas body Ukrgaz in charge of future imports from Turkmenistan.
Ukraine owes about another $200 million for gas delivered by the Central Asian former Soviet republic of Turkmenistan before 1996.
The decision to postpone Kuchma's trip could be a blow to Ukraine's plans to reduce its dependency on Russia for energy supplies.
Ukraine was due to import 11.1 billion cubic metres of natural gas from Turkmenistan in 1997.
There are also plans to import another 53 billion cubic metres of Russian gas from state gas monopoly Gazprom GAZP.RTS, and 10 billion cubic metres from Uzbekistan.
Kuchma had been due to sign 11 documents which had already been initialled, including a long-term deal on gas imports, Interfax said.
